clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old male with 20 pack-year smoking history (quit 3 months prior) presented to the emergency department with nausea and vomiting occurring 3-4 times daily for 3 days. Physical examination revealed mild right upper lung field end-expiratory wheezing. Initial laboratory studies demonstrated severe hyponatremia (sodium 110 mEq/L on day 1, improving to 119 on day 2, 130 on day 6) with low serum osmolality (227 mOsm/kg) and high urine osmolality (579 mOsm/kg), consistent with syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH). High urine sodium (126 mEq/L) and normal ACTH, cortisol, and TSH ruled out other causes of hyponatremia. Chest X-ray showed no acute cardiopulmonary disease. Subsequent chest CT revealed a 3.0 × 1.9 cm conglomeration of nodules in the inferior segment of the right upper lobe with ipsilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy. CT-guided percutaneous biopsy confirmed small cell lung cancer histology with positive immunostaining for CK, CD56, NSE, Synaptophysin, PAX-5, and TTF-1, and negative staining for Chromogranin, CD57, and NFP. The patient was classified as having limited-stage SCLC and was initiated on chemotherapy with plans for subsequent prophylactic cranial irradiation.
